name: Macro-regime-gated reversion — buy dips only in a risk-on macro regime (long spot)
rationale: REGIME-SWITCHING: a macro regime SELECTS whether a sub-strategy (here mean-reversion) is allowed to fire. Mean-reversion dip-buying works in benign regimes and is a catastrophe in a macro de-risking (every dip keeps dipping). macro_regime is a FRED-derived composite (curve slope, real rates, liquidity) that tags the shared cross-asset risk regime — exactly the switch that should turn dip-buying ON only when the macro backdrop supports a bounce. Mechanism before data: long spot when macro_regime is above a fitted risk-on floor (benign backdrop) AND price is oversold (RSI below a fitted floor — the dip); exit on RSI recovery or barriers. This is a true regime-conditional strategy: the SAME oversold trigger is gated by an orthogonal MACRO state, distinct from rsi-dip-buy-in-an-uptrend (gated by the asset's OWN trend + realized vol, no macro), funding-reset-reversion (funding gate), and reg-risk-derisk-momentum (regulatory index gating MOMENTUM, not reversion). Disconfirmer 1: drop the macro_regime gate — if bare oversold dip-buying matches the deflated Sharpe, the macro regime adds nothing. Disconfirmer 2: macro_regime is slow (next-day FRED, infrequent updates); if it changes so rarely it is a near-constant over the sample, it is not actually selecting regimes — the gate's behaviour-vs-control comparison will show it. Disconfirmer 3 (PIT/cost): FRED next-day-available; net of ~20bps the reversion must clear. tier0 macro_regime + tier0 rsi, fresh-enough prod data, unproven combination — low-confidence until OOS.
catalyst: oversold price (the dip) gated to fire ONLY when the FRED macro regime is risk-on (benign backdrop) — regime-conditional reversion, long spot
